general.summary: CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption flaw in Open Java Development Kit’s Base64 decoder, can allow unauthenticated attackers to run code on servers hosting widely used Java applications. Nicknamed “Java4Shell” by Calif, the company whose researchers found it, CVE-2026-114938 was fixed by Oracle and the OpenJDK project on Tuesday. There is currently no evidence of successful attacks leveraging the flaw, but the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) “strongly urges” organizations to patch immediately.
